deep_dive.title: CellRFT: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Single-Cell Perturbation Modeling
deep_dive.abstract: Predicting cellular responses to perturbations supports the study of gene function, disease mechanisms, and therapeutic strategies. Despite advances in single-cell perturbation modeling, existing models typically optimize surrogate losses that do not directly reflect the biological criteria used for evaluation, so better data fitting need not yield better biological predictions. To address this mismatch, we introduce \textbf{CellRFT}, a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that uses biological evaluation as direct training feedback. CellRFT uses policy-gradient optimization to learn from non-differentiable evaluations of generated cell populations and integrates multiple biological rewards through hierarchical reward aggregation. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate CellRFT's applicability across different pretrained models and effectiveness in improving perturbation prediction, reveal that optimizing one biological criterion can help or hinder others, and show that complementary rewards can improve criteria beyond those directly optimized, offering a way to probe how biological metrics shape model behavior, with the potential to inform evaluation design. Code will be made available.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Existing single-cell perturbation models optimize surrogate losses misaligned with biological criteria. CellRFT introduces reinforcement fine-tuning that uses biological evaluation as direct training feedback, improving cellular perturbation response prediction.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 现有单细胞扰动响应预测模型多优化代理损失，与生物学评价标准不一致，导致拟合更好未必预测更准。本文提出CellRFT强化微调框架，以生物学评价作为直接训练反馈，通过策略梯度从不可微的细胞群评估中学习，并用分层奖励聚合整合多种生物奖励。综合实验表明该方法在扰动响应预测上取得更契合生物学标准的性能，为虚拟细胞建模提供了以生物反馈为导向的新训练范式。

quick_skim.title: One Intervention per Component is Enough: Towards Identifiability in Linear Stochastic Dynamics from Steady State
quick_skim.abstract: We study the problem of recovering the parameters of a multivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process from steady-state observational and interventional data. In many applications, such as large-scale gene perturbation experiments, only stationary "snapshot" measurements are available, making standard stochastic differential equation estimation methods that rely on time-series trajectories inapplicable. We first establish an identifiability result: one intervention per strongly connected component (SCC) of the drift graph suffices to recover all OU process parameters generically up to a global scaling factor. This holds provided that the SCC condensation graph is connected with a single root and certain spectral nondegeneracy assumptions hold. We propose a recursive learning algorithm that orders SCCs topologically and, for each component, isolates its marginal dynamics and solves a linear system derived from the steady-state moment equations, leveraging parameters recovered for upstream components. Building on this theoretical foundation, we propose a regularized least-squares estimator that jointly minimizes residuals of the steady-state mean and covariance equations across observational and interventional data. Experimental results validate our theoretical findings in recovering parameters of the underlying OU process.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Standard SDE estimation needs time series, but gene perturbation data give only steady-state snapshots. This work proves one intervention per strongly connected component suffices to recover Ornstein-Uhlenbeck parameters up to scaling, enabling perturbation modeling from interventional snapshots.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 许多基因扰动实验只能获得稳态快照，传统依赖时间序列的随机微分方程估计方法因此失效。该文针对多元Ornstein-Uhlenbeck过程，研究如何从稳态观测与干预数据中恢复参数，并证明对漂移图的每个强连通分量施加一次干预即可在全局缩放意义下唯一辨识全部参数。结果为从静态扰动数据建模调控网络提供了可识别性理论保证。
